name: Daffodil
latin: Narcissus (garden hybrids, from N. pseudonarcissus and others)
grown_as: Drawn as the classic golden yellow trumpet daffodil of UK gardens. ⚠️ CHECK: William's library has three daffodils, none of them a plain trumpet: 'Tête-à-tête' (dwarf, all yellow, often two or three flowers to a stem), 'Golden Echo' (several flowers to a stem, white petals and a long yellow cup) and 'Delnashaugh' (a double, white with apricot-pink). He also has the wild daffodil, N. pseudonarcissus, in the orchard, which is smaller with pale yellow petals and a deeper yellow trumpet. Which of these the drawing should be is for William.
habit: Clumps of upright grey-green leaves 20 to 40 cm high, each bulb with one leafless flower stem about as tall as the leaves. Clumps widen year by year as bulbs divide.

leaf.arrangement: Two to four leaves from the base of each bulb, upright then arching, wrapped at the bottom in a papery sheath
leaf.outline: Long and narrow, 20 to 40 cm by 8 to 15 mm, the same width nearly all the way
leaf.base: Running down into the sheath at soil level
leaf.veins: Fine parallel veins along the length
leaf.surface: Flat or shallowly channelled, smooth, grey-green with a waxy bloom

flower.form: A trumpet (the corona) sticking out from a flat star of six petals, held sideways
flower.petals: Six tepals, joined at the base into a short tube, spreading flat or swept slightly forward, oval and pointed, overlapping a little. The trumpet in the middle is as long as the tepals or longer, with a frilled, flared rim.
flower.colour: Golden yellow; the trumpet the same or a shade deeper
flower.centre: Inside the trumpet six stamens and a style, hidden from the side. Behind the tepals the green swollen ovary.
flower.behind: A thin brown papery spathe (sheath) at the bend where the stem turns
flower.carried: One flower per stem, held sideways or a little nodding, at the top of a leafless, flattened, two-edged stem that bends just below the flower

fruit: A green, three-sided swelling behind the dead petals, about 1.5 to 2 cm, ripening to a brown papery capsule that splits into three and drops round black seeds. Usually removed by deadheading.
seedling: Not drawn. A single grass-like leaf; five years or more to flower.
winter: Nothing above ground until the blunt leaf tips appear in January or February.

leaf: one long strap-shaped leaf, even width
bloom: six pointed tepals in a flat star
a long trumpet with a frilled rim in the middle, as long as the tepals
yellow all over, the trumpet a shade deeper
a papery brown sheath at the bend of the stem behind it
bulb: a large teardrop bulb 4 to 6 cm with a pointed nose
roots from a flat base plate, often a side bulb attached
shoots: blunt grey-green leaf tips coming up in a tight bunch
a fat flower bud in a papery sheath rising between them
flower: one sideways-facing trumpet flower per stem, about as tall as the leaves
seedhead: green swollen pods behind withered papery petals
leaves still green, starting to flop
dormant: yellowing, flopped leaves or nothing above the soil

look_alikes: Other kinds of daffodil differ in the cup (short in large-cupped and jonquil types) or flowers to a stem. Wild daffodil is smaller with pale petals and a darker trumpet. Leaves alone look like bluebell (glossy, darker green, hooded tip) or snowdrop (much narrower).
